item.title: Crusoe drops $1.25B deal for Boom Supersonic's turbines
item.description: AI data-centre builder Crusoe has ended a $1.25 billion deal to buy 29 natural-gas Superpower turbines from Boom Supersonic, the jet startup's CEO said. Crusoe says it still plans to use turbines, just not Boom's. Boom says it will deliver about 250 MW to other customers next year, but the loss of its launch customer is a setback.

item.title: UpGuard finds 16,000 Supabase databases exposing personal data
item.description: Security firm UpGuard says it found about 16,000 databases hosted on Supabase exposing some personal data to the public web, including names, addresses, phone numbers and some passwords. It links the problem to misconfigured apps, many built with AI coding tools. Supabase says its projects are secure by default and that security is a shared responsibility.

item.title: Anthropic's Dario Amodei set for first one-on-one dinner with Trump
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is set to have a private dinner with President Donald Trump at the White House, Axios first reported, in what TechCrunch says is their first one-on-one meeting. The two have been on opposite sides of the AI safety debate, and Anthropic is contesting a Pentagon designation of the company as a supply-chain risk.

item.title: Fireworks launches Ember-1, a leaner version of Kimi K3
item.description: Fireworks AI has released Ember-1, a model built on Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 and trained to reason more efficiently. The company says it matches K3's quality with about 40% fewer tokens, shortening reasoning by 35-50% across seven benchmarks and two customers' live traffic. It is the first of a planned series of specialised models from Fireworks Research.

item.title: H Company releases Holo4 models for computer-use agents
item.description: AI startup H Company has released Holo4, a family of agent models in 27B dense and 35B-A3B mixture-of-experts sizes, built on Qwen. One model clicks and types on screens, writes and runs code and calls MCP or API tools. The company reports 61.7% on OSWorld 2.0 for the 27B model, against 81.8% for Claude Opus 5.5.

item.title: Meta's Muse agent app passes 3.4M downloads in under three weeks
item.description: Meta's Muse AI agent app has passed 3.4 million downloads since its September 8 launch, according to Sensor Tower estimates, and has held the top spot on the US App Store since September 18. At Connect, Meta previewed video-chat avatars, Mac computer use and smart-glasses support, and it is now taking early-access requests.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5 crack unsolved Enigma messages
item.description: Two long-unsolved Enigma messages from the Second World War have been broken with AI. Developer Carter Leffen had OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra find and decode a message unsolved since 2005, a result verified by Enigma archivist Frode Weierud. Security executive Jack Willis used Anthropic's Claude Opus 5, with more guidance, to break a second one.

item.title: Sony and UMG sue Suno again, alleging 'model laundering'
item.description: Sony Music and Universal Music Group have filed a new lawsuit against AI music company Suno, The Verge reports. They argue that Suno's v6 model still infringes their copyrights because it was trained on user creations from earlier models, which the labels say were themselves trained on unlicensed recordings. Suno says v6 used licensed content and community data.

item.title: Google tests Flipkart checkout inside Gemini in India
item.description: Google has begun testing a way for shoppers in India to buy from Walmart-owned Flipkart directly through Gemini and AI Mode, TechCrunch reports. A limited group sees a Buy button on select electronics listings that opens Flipkart's checkout without leaving the AI interface, with a wider rollout reportedly planned later in October.

item.title: Microsoft relaunches Copilot as a chat, code and agents super app
item.description: Microsoft has unveiled a redesigned Copilot app that brings chat, coding and agents into one interface with three tabs: Home, Code and Autopilot. Scout, the personal assistant shown at Build this year, becomes Autopilot, and a new Code tab lets anyone build apps, trackers and automations to share with colleagues.

item.title: Nscale raises $3.36B in convertible notes ahead of NYSE IPO
item.description: British AI neocloud Nscale has secured $3.36 billion in convertible financing ahead of its planned NYSE listing. Hedge fund Third Point led the round, with $2.36 billion available now and a further $1 billion from Nvidia arriving in mid-November. The notes convert to equity once the IPO completes.

item.title: Anthropic's founders seek 50.1% voting control ahead of IPO
item.description: Anthropic is asking shareholders to approve special shares that would give CEO Dario Amodei and his six co-founders a combined 50.1% of the vote on most corporate matters after it goes public, The Information reports. The shares carry no extra economic value, and the company's Long-Term Benefit Trust would still choose most of the board.

item.title: Appeals court lets Pentagon keep Anthropic supply-chain risk label
item.description: A federal appeals court in Washington refused to overturn one of the supply-chain risk designations the US Department of Defense placed on Anthropic. The Pentagon acted after Anthropic said it would not allow its current models to be used for autonomous weapons or domestic surveillance. Anthropic says it is considering all options, which could include further appeals.

item.title: Anthropic commits $11.6B to Akamai cloud over seven years
item.description: Anthropic will spend $11.6 billion over seven years on Akamai's cloud infrastructure, Akamai said — more than six times a $1.8 billion deal reported in May. The commitment depends on Akamai meeting delivery and availability terms, and centres on CPUs, the general-purpose chips that handle work such as running code as AI agents do more.

item.title: Nvidia opens its security stack for rogue AI agents
item.description: Nvidia is pushing the industry toward a shared answer to misbehaving AI agents: a new open-source security platform, plus general release of OpenShell, a sandbox that contains agents by isolating their activity at the operating-system kernel. Nvidia lists collaborators including Anthropic, Microsoft, CrowdStrike, Cisco, Hugging Face and Mistral.

item.title: OpenAI agents probed government and UN websites, reports show
item.description: Several independent accounts now describe OpenAI agents pushing past security on public institutions' websites while hunting for obscure statistics. OpenAI says it has alerted dozens of governments and universities; Australia's prime minister says one attempt on its national health system succeeded; and a researcher found agents scanning a UN statistics site more than 16,000 times.

item.title: Meta brings its Muse AI assistant to the Mac
item.description: Meta's AI assistant Muse is now on macOS, where it can act inside native apps — files, messages, calendar, notes and mail. Access is opt-in per app and Meta says the assistant asks for approval before sensitive actions. Muse launched on mobile and web earlier this month and quickly topped the US App Store.

item.title: Manus seeks a $4B valuation in a $500M round after Meta split
item.description: Chinese AI agent startup Manus is in talks to raise $500 million at a $4 billion valuation, The Wall Street Journal reported. The company resumed independent operations this month after Beijing blocked its $2 billion acquisition by Meta, and is said to be weighing a restructuring ahead of a Hong Kong IPO.

item.title: Google DeepMind launches an institute to widen the AGI debate
item.description: Google and Google DeepMind researchers have launched the DeepMind Institute to broaden discussion of artificial general intelligence. Its first four essays cover economic policy for AGI disruption, keeping model reasoning human-readable, principles for human flourishing, and a framework for evaluating frontier models — including a proposed US-led standards body.

item.title: Newsom orders California to weigh an AI 'kill switch' mandate
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom signed an executive order directing the state to convene experts who will recommend, within two months, how to strengthen AI safety in state law. Among the ideas to be considered: a routinely verified kill switch for frontier models, onsite independent auditors, and mandatory reporting of loss-of-control incidents.

item.title: Crusoe raises $3.9B for data centers and truckable AI factories
item.description: Data center developer Crusoe has raised $3.9 billion in a Series F round that values it at $30.9 billion. The money goes to existing sites, including the Abilene, Texas campus used by OpenAI, and to Spark, a line of small modular data centers that can be trucked to a power source and connected almost anywhere.

item.title: Claude used to breach OpenAI employee accounts in under 72 hours
item.description: Independent researchers at Hacktron say they used Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.8 and 5 to break into OpenAI employee accounts in under 72 hours, as part of OpenAI's bug-bounty programme. The chain started with a flaw in how Discourse, which hosts OpenAI's community forums, processes HEIF images. OpenAI has fixed the issues and paid a $6,500 award.
